bull: Profit of $4.23 per share beat what analysts expected, and was up from $3.52 the quarter before.

bear: The stock fell about 4% on November 2 as oil prices dropped more than 7%.
Peace talks between the US and Iran could keep pushing oil prices down.

Even so, the stock fell about 8% to 9% because the company gave a cautious outlook and still faces about $2.2 billion in tariff costs this year.

bear: The stock dropped about 9% on the day of the report, after already falling 13% in the month before.
Tariffs (taxes on imported goods) will cost Caterpillar about $2.2 billion this year.
Caterpillar can't build machines fast enough to meet demand, which limits how quickly the backlog turns into sales.

briefs.headline: Disney stock inches up as it cuts costs and pays big to hire AI workers
briefs.summary: Disney shares were trading near $113 on October 22, up a bit more than 2% from the week before. New CEO Josh D'Amaro is reshaping the company. Disney is merging its TV and streaming teams, raising prices for Disney+ and Hulu without ads, and cutting more jobs to make more money. Disney also agreed to pay $60 million a year to hire 66 workers from Character.AI, an AI chatbot company that has gone bankrupt (meaning it can't pay its debts), while one research firm lowered its guess for where Disney's stock is headed.
bull: In its last quarterly report, Disney brought in $25.25 billion in sales, up 6.8% from a year earlier, and its profit per share beat what experts expected.
Disney's cost cutting and price increases are meant to help it keep more of the money it makes.
Hiring Character.AI's workers and getting rights to its technology gives Disney more AI know-how under its new CEO's plan.
bear: Research firm Arete lowered its price target (its guess of what the stock should be worth) from $88 to $86, about 24% below where the stock was trading.
Disney will spend about $180 million over three years on the AI workers' pay and bonuses to keep them, right after laying off several hundred of its own staff.
Character.AI has faced lawsuits from families saying its chatbots hurt their teens, and one market expert said investors now want to see real results.
briefs.nextEvent: Disney reports its full-year and fourth-quarter 2026 results on November 17, 2026, before the stock market opens.

briefs.headline: Bitcoin stays near $77,000 as fund outflows and Binance withdrawals continue
briefs.summary: Bitcoin traded around $76,300 to $78,250 on Tuesday, November 3, and was down about 3% by midday at around $77,600. Bitcoin funds that trade like stocks (ETFs) lost about $399 million on Monday, their second day in a row of money leaving. Customers have now pulled a net $4.72 billion from Binance, the biggest crypto exchange, since it reopened after hackers stole about $6.3 billion on October 29. Traders also expected bigger price swings around the US midterm elections.
bull: Binance says it has replaced about 95% of the stolen money, and it reopened more withdrawals on Tuesday.
Binance posted a new proof that its customers' coins are backed at least one-for-one.
Bitcoin bounced back from its low near $76,300 and stayed above a key level traders watch.
bear: BlackRock's bitcoin fund lost $405 million on Monday, its biggest one-day outflow since June.
A fear gauge for crypto (the Fear and Greed index) dropped, showing investors are nervous.
New hacks hit other exchanges, like about $40 million taken from Brazil's Mercado Bitcoin.

briefs.summary: Ethereum (ETH) traded around $2,290 on Tuesday, November 3, up about 0.6% early in the day, after dipping below $2,200 during the sell-off that followed the $6.3 billion Binance hack. Many traders bought options that pay off if the price falls (called puts), with the most popular betting on a drop to $1,900 by Friday. Binance reopened withdrawals for stablecoins (coins tied to the US dollar) on the Ethereum network first on Tuesday.
bull: Ethereum did a little better than Bitcoin, and its price compared with Bitcoin edged up.
Binance says it has replaced about 95% of the stolen money and is reopening withdrawals step by step.
Ethereum bounced back from below $2,200 and stayed above that level, which traders watch closely.
bear: Money kept leaving Ethereum funds, with about $482 million pulled out in five trading days.
Traders are betting on drops: the six most-traded Ethereum options were all bets that the price will fall.
Hackers could sell stolen coins through Ethereum-based markets, which could push the price down.
